otherDetail: Interest expense of $53M on AppLovin's debt, partly offset by $8M of other income — and a $147M loss from the apps business AppLovin sold in June, which accounting rules report as discontinued operations. That loss includes a $189M write-down of the apps business's goodwill ahead of the sale.

segments.name: Advertising platform
segments.note: Ads placed through AppLovin's AXON platform — advertisers pay to reach users inside other companies' apps, and AXON's AI decides which ads to show. AppLovin sold its own apps business in June 2025; its results sit in discontinued operations, below.

sources.label: Q2 2025 release — restated continuing-operations statements (SEC EDGAR)

takeaways.text: Revenue from the AXON advertising platform rose 71% from a year ago to $1.16B, and the continuing business turned that into $840M of operating income — a 72% operating margin, because the platform's costs barely grow with its sales.
takeaways.title: The platform kept compounding

takeaways.text: In February AppLovin agreed to sell its own games/apps business. Writing that business's goodwill down by $189M ahead of the sale drove a $147M discontinued-operations loss — the reason reported net income ($576M) is well below the platform's own earnings ($724M).
takeaways.title: A goodwill write-down on the way out

takeaways.text: Adjusted EBITDA — profit before interest, tax and non-cash charges — was $938M, 81 cents of every revenue dollar. Few companies anywhere convert sales into cash profit at that rate.
takeaways.title: Cash generation stayed extreme

verdict: AppLovin's ad platform grew revenue 71% to $1.16B and earned $724M from its continuing business — but a $147M loss from the apps business it was about to sell, including a $189M goodwill write-down, held reported net income to $576M.
